extra_notes.Hunger (self-reported): These answers come straight from the household. They are strongly linked to poverty, but in a real registration system people could easily change their answers to pay less.
extra_notes.Sensitive characteristics: Religion may make predictions more accurate, but charging people differently because of their religion would be discriminatory. Is a more accurate model always a fairer one?
extra_notes.Everyday household items: Cheap items that almost all households own (or don't). Do they tell the model anything new?
extra_notes.Electrical goods: Items that usually signal electricity access and higher spending.
extra_notes.Livelihood: How the household makes a living.
extra_notes.Who lives here: Simple counts that the model only captures indirectly.
extra_notes.Work: About the household head's main job. Most informal workers have no contract or benefits.
